audit_status.source_base: Greek Romans text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Paul's grief, Israel privileges, promise/election, mercy, potter imagery, remnant, nations attaining righteousness/justice, stumbling stone. Anti-Jewish use must be rejected.

verses.restored: I speak truth in Messiah; I do not lie, my conscience bearing witness together with me in holy Spirit,

familiar.text: I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Ghost,

modern.text: I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as confirmed by my conscience in the Holy Spirit.

original.text: Ἀλήθειαν λέγω ἐν Χριστῷ, οὐ ψεύδομαι, συμμαρτυρούσης μοι τῆς συνειδήσεώς μου ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ,

verses.restored: that there is great grief for me and unceasing pain in my heart.

familiar.text: That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart.

modern.text: I have deep sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.

original.text: ὅτι λύπη μοί ἐστιν μεγάλη καὶ ἀδιάλειπτος ὀδύνη τῇ καρδίᾳ μου·

verses.restored: For I could pray that I myself be accursed away from Messiah for my siblings, my kin according to flesh,

familiar.text: For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh:

modern.text: For I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my own flesh and blood,

original.text: ηὐχόμην γὰρ ⸂ἀνάθεμα εἶναι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ⸃ ἀπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν συγγενῶν μου κατὰ σάρκα,

verses.restored: who are Israelites, whose are the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the Law, the service, and the promises,

familiar.text: Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises;

modern.text: the people of Israel. Theirs is the adoption as sons; theirs the divine glory and the covenants; theirs the giving of the law, the temple worship, and the promises.

original.text: οἵτινές εἰσιν Ἰσραηλῖται, ὧν ἡ υἱοθεσία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ αἱ διαθῆκαι καὶ ἡ νομοθεσία καὶ ἡ λατρεία καὶ αἱ ἐπαγγελίαι,

verses.restored: whose are the fathers, and from whom is the Messiah according to flesh, the One over all, Divine blessed into the ages. Amen.

familiar.text: Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.

modern.text: Theirs are the patriarchs, and from them proceeds the human descent of Christ, who is God over all, forever worthy of praise! Amen. God’s Sovereign Choice (Genesis 25:19–28; Malachi 1:1–5)

original.text: ὧν οἱ πατέρες, καὶ ἐξ ὧν ὁ χριστὸς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, ὁ ὢν ἐπὶ πάντων, θεὸς εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.

verses.restored: But it is not as though the word of the Divine has fallen. For not all those from Israel are Israel,

familiar.text: Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel:

modern.text: It is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.

original.text: Οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι ἐκπέπτωκεν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ. οὐ γὰρ πάντες οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραήλ, οὗτοι Ἰσραήλ·

verses.restored: nor because they are seed of Abraham are all children, but: In Isaac your seed will be called.

familiar.text: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.

modern.text: Nor because they are Abraham’s descendants are they all his children. On the contrary, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”

original.text: οὐδʼ ὅτι εἰσὶν σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ, πάντες τέκνα, ἀλλʼ· Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα.

verses.restored: That is, not the children of flesh, these are children of the Divine, but the children of the promise are counted as seed.

familiar.text: That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

modern.text: So it is not the children of the flesh who are God’s children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring.

original.text: τοῦτʼ ἔστιν, οὐ τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκὸς ταῦτα τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐπαγγελίας λογίζεται εἰς σπέρμα·

verses.restored: For the word of promise is this: According to this season I will come, and Sarah will have a son.

familiar.text: For this is the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son.

modern.text: For this is what the promise stated: “At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son.”

original.text: ἐπαγγελίας γὰρ ὁ λόγος οὗτος· Κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον ἐλεύσομαι καὶ ἔσται τῇ Σάρρᾳ υἱός.

verses.restored: And not only this, but also Rebecca, having conception from one, Isaac our father—

familiar.text: And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac;

modern.text: Not only that, but Rebecca’s children were conceived by one man, our father Isaac.

original.text: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ Ῥεβέκκα ἐξ ἑνὸς κοίτην ἔχουσα, Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν·

verses.restored: for though they were not yet born nor had practiced anything good or harmful, so that the purpose of the Divine according to choosing might remain, not from works but from the One calling—

familiar.text: (For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;)

modern.text: Yet before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad, in order that God’s plan of election might stand,

original.text: μήπω γὰρ γεννηθέντων μηδὲ πραξάντων τι ἀγαθὸν ἢ ⸀φαῦλον, ἵνα ἡ κατʼ ἐκλογὴν πρόθεσις τοῦ θεοῦ μένῃ,

verses.restored: it was said to her, The greater will serve the lesser.

familiar.text: It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger.

modern.text: not by works but by Him who calls, she was told, “The older will serve the younger.”

original.text: οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἀλλʼ ἐκ τοῦ καλοῦντος, ἐρρέθη αὐτῇ ὅτι Ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι·

verses.restored: Just as it is written: Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.

familiar.text: As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.

modern.text: So it is written: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”

original.text: ⸀καθὼς γέγραπται· Τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἠγάπησα, τὸν δὲ Ἠσαῦ ἐμίσησα.

verses.restored: What then shall we say? Is there injustice with the Divine? May it not be.

familiar.text: What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid.

modern.text: What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Certainly not!

original.text: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; μὴ ἀδικία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ; μὴ γένοιτο·

verses.restored: For to Moses he says, I will show mercy to whom I show mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.

familiar.text: For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.

modern.text: For He says to Moses: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”

original.text: τῷ ⸂Μωϋσεῖ γὰρ⸃ λέγει· Ἐλεήσω ὃν ἂν ἐλεῶ, καὶ οἰκτιρήσω ὃν ἂν οἰκτίρω.

verses.restored: So then it is not of the one willing nor of the one running, but of the Divine showing mercy.

familiar.text: So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.

modern.text: So then, it does not depend on man’s desire or effort, but on God’s mercy.

original.text: ἄρα οὖν οὐ τοῦ θέλοντος οὐδὲ τοῦ τρέχοντος ἀλλὰ τοῦ ἐλεῶντος θεοῦ.

verses.restored: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: For this very thing I raised you up, so that I might show in you my power, and so that my name might be announced in all the earth.

familiar.text: For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.

modern.text: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: “I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power in you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”

original.text: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ τῷ Φαραὼ ὅτι Εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἐξήγειρά σε ὅπως ἐνδείξωμαι ἐν σοὶ τὴν δύναμίν μου, καὶ ὅπως διαγγελῇ τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ.

verses.restored: So then, whom he wills he shows mercy, and whom he wills he hardens.

familiar.text: Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth.

modern.text: Therefore God has mercy on whom He wants to have mercy, and He hardens whom He wants to harden.

original.text: ἄρα οὖν ὃν θέλει ἐλεεῖ, ὃν δὲ θέλει σκληρύνει.

verses.restored: You will say to me then, Why does he still find fault? For who has resisted his will?

familiar.text: Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will?

modern.text: One of you will say to me, “Then why does God still find fault? For who can resist His will?”

original.text: Ἐρεῖς ⸂μοι οὖν⸃· Τί ⸀οὖν ἔτι μέμφεται; τῷ γὰρ βουλήματι αὐτοῦ τίς ἀνθέστηκεν;

verses.restored: O human, rather, who are you answering back to the Divine? Will what is formed say to the one forming it, Why did you make me this way?

familiar.text: Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?

modern.text: But who are you, O man, to talk back to God? Shall what is formed say to Him who formed it, “Why did You make me like this?”

original.text: ⸂ὦ ἄνθρωπε, μενοῦνγε⸃ σὺ τίς εἶ ὁ ἀνταποκρινόμενος τῷ θεῷ; μὴ ἐρεῖ τὸ πλάσμα τῷ πλάσαντι Τί με ἐποίησας οὕτως;

verses.restored: Or does not the potter have authority over the clay, from the same lump to make one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?

familiar.text: Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?

modern.text: Does not the potter have the right to make from the same lump of clay one vessel for special occasions and another for common use?

original.text: ἢ οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν ὁ κεραμεὺς τοῦ πηλοῦ ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ φυράματος ποιῆσαι ὃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν σκεῦος ὃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν;

verses.restored: But if the Divine, willing to show wrath and make known his power, bore with much patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction,

familiar.text: What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction:

modern.text: What if God, intending to show His wrath and make His power known, bore with great patience the vessels of His wrath, prepared for destruction?

original.text: εἰ δὲ θέλων ὁ θεὸς ἐνδείξασθαι τὴν ὀργὴν καὶ γνωρίσαι τὸ δυνατὸν αὐτοῦ ἤνεγκεν ἐν πολλῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σκεύη ὀργῆς κατηρτισμένα εἰς ἀπώλειαν,

verses.restored: and so that he might make known the riches of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory,

familiar.text: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory,

modern.text: What if He did this to make the riches of His glory known to the vessels of His mercy, whom He prepared in advance for glory—

original.text: ⸀καὶ ἵνα γνωρίσῃ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ σκεύη ἐλέους, ἃ προητοίμασεν εἰς δόξαν,

verses.restored: even us whom he called, not only from Judeans but also from nations?

familiar.text: Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?

modern.text: including us, whom He has called not only from the Jews, but also from the Gentiles?

original.text: οὓς καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς οὐ μόνον ἐξ Ἰουδαίων ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἐθνῶν;—

verses.restored: As also in Hosea he says: I will call the not-my-people, my people, and the not-beloved, beloved.

familiar.text: As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.

modern.text: As He says in Hosea: “I will call them ‘My People’ who are not My people, and I will call her ‘My Beloved’ who is not My beloved,”

original.text: ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ὡσηὲ λέγει· Καλέσω τὸν οὐ λαόν μου λαόν μου καὶ τὴν οὐκ ἠγαπημένην ἠγαπημένην·

verses.restored: And it will be, in the place where it was said to them, You are not my people, there they will be called sons/children of the living Divine.

familiar.text: And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.

modern.text: and, “It will happen that in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’”

original.text: καὶ ἔσται ἐν τῷ τόπῳ οὗ ἐρρέθη ⸀αὐτοῖς· Οὐ λαός μου ὑμεῖς, ἐκεῖ κληθήσονται υἱοὶ θεοῦ ζῶντος.

verses.restored: And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved/healed,

familiar.text: Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved:

modern.text: Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: “Though the number of the Israelites is like the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved.

original.text: Ἠσαΐας δὲ κράζει ὑπὲρ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ· Ἐὰν ᾖ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης, τὸ ⸀ὑπόλειμμα σωθήσεται·

verses.restored: for the Lord will complete and cut short the word upon the earth.

familiar.text: For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth.

modern.text: For the Lord will carry out His sentence on the earth thoroughly and decisively.”

original.text: λόγον γὰρ συντελῶν καὶ ⸀συντέμνων ποιήσει κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

verses.restored: And just as Isaiah said beforehand: Unless Lord Sabaoth had left us seed, we would have become like Sodom and been made like Gomorrah.

familiar.text: And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha.

modern.text: It is just as Isaiah foretold: “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.” Israel’s Unbelief

original.text: καὶ καθὼς προείρηκεν Ἠσαΐας· Εἰ μὴ κύριος Σαβαὼθ ἐγκατέλιπεν ἡμῖν σπέρμα, ὡς Σόδομα ἂν ἐγενήθημεν καὶ ὡς Γόμορρα ἂν ὡμοιώθημεν.

verses.restored: What then shall we say? That nations not pursuing righteousness/justice attained righteousness/justice, but righteousness/justice from trust;

familiar.text: What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith.

modern.text: What then will we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith;

original.text: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ὅτι ἔθνη τὰ μὴ διώκοντα δικαιοσύνην κατέλαβεν δικαιοσύνην, δικαιοσύνην δὲ τὴν ἐκ πίστεως·

verses.restored: but Israel, pursuing a Law of righteousness/justice, did not arrive at that Law.

familiar.text: But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness.

modern.text: but Israel, who pursued a law of righteousness, has not attained it.

original.text: Ἰσραὴλ δὲ διώκων νόμον δικαιοσύνης εἰς ⸀νόμον οὐκ ἔφθασεν.

verses.restored: Why? Because not from trust but as from works. They stumbled over the stone of stumbling,

familiar.text: Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone;

modern.text: Why not? Because their pursuit was not by faith, but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone,

original.text: διὰ τί; ὅτι οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως ἀλλʼ ὡς ἐξ ⸀ἔργων· ⸀προσέκοψαν τῷ λίθῳ τοῦ προσκόμματος,

verses.restored: just as it is written: Look, I place in Zion a stone of stumbling and rock of offense, and the one trusting upon him will not be put to shame.

familiar.text: As it is written, Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence: and whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

modern.text: as it is written: “See, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”

original.text: καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἰδοὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον προσκόμματος καὶ πέτραν σκανδάλου, ⸀καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται.

safety_note: Romans 9 must not be used as replacement theology or anti-Jewish rhetoric. Paul begins with grief and honor for Israel's gifts, and the argument continues through Romans 10-11 toward mercy, not erasure.
